summary: Billing/Usage spike — customer suspects double-count after increased retries on streaming
description:
Customer reports a sudden increase in billed usage (tokens + request count) starting ~2026-02-10 21:00 UTC. Customer suspects double-counting because they did not intentionally increase traffic.

Impact
- Customer reports ~2.1x increase in daily token usage compared to prior 7-day average.
- Concern about invoice / budget thresholds; asking if Redwood is double-counting streaming requests.

Customer context
- Company: Aurora Search (Hosted API / self_serve)
- Workload: chat completions with streaming enabled; TS SDK
- Recent changes (per customer): upgraded SDK + added more aggressive retry logic due to intermittent timeouts.

Initial intake (Support)
Requested:
- Workspace/org ID
- Example request IDs from before/after spike (minimum 10 each)
- Endpoint(s): /v1/chat/completions vs /v1/completions; streaming on/off
- SDK version + any custom retry settings (max_retries, timeout, backoff)
- Whether they are retrying on stream disconnects / client timeouts
- Whether they have idempotency keys enabled (if applicable)

Investigation checklist (metering + retries + streaming)
1) Metering sanity checks (internal)
- Compare usage by endpoint/model/region for the day of spike vs baseline.
- Validate metering pipeline health (lag/backfill) to rule out delayed ingestion.
- Spot-check raw metering events for a sample of request IDs (ensure one billable event per request ID).
- Confirm token accounting rules for streaming: tokens are counted on tokens generated, not on reconnect attempts unless a new generation occurred.

2) Retry/dedup checks
- Look for repeated prompts with near-identical input + short inter-arrival time (possible client retry loops).
- Check error distribution leading up to retries (499/504, stream resets, gateway timeouts, client timeouts).
- Verify whether customer retries are creating *new* request IDs (expected) vs same ID (rare).

3) Streaming-specific checks
- Confirm whether customer uses reconnect/resume logic that replays the entire request on disconnect.
- Confirm client timeout/keepalive settings and whether they sit behind a proxy that may cut idle streams.

4) Billing hooks / metering duplication hypothesis
- If sample request IDs show multiple metering events per request ID, escalate to Billing/Metering owner with:
  - request_id list
  - org_id
  - timestamps
  - metering event IDs (if available)
  - expected vs observed counts

Notes / constraints
- Avoid sharing internal event schemas or customer-unsafe identifiers in external comms.
- If customer is approaching a spend cap, coordinate with CS on temporary limit adjustments (no promises on credits without approvals).
comments: 2026-02-11 17:22Z (Dev Patel): Opened per Aurora Search report of billing usage spike. Asked for org ID + sample request IDs + SDK version + retry settings + whether streaming is enabled. Set priority P2 pending confirmation of impact magnitude.

2026-02-11 19:05Z (Customer - Aurora Search): Confirmed streaming enabled for most traffic. Recently bumped retries from 2 -> 6 and lowered client timeout to 20s due to occasional slow responses. Provided 15 request IDs from 2026-02-10/11 and notes that many requests appear to “restart” after a timeout.

2026-02-12 00:40Z (Priya Shah): Internal usage dashboard review: request count increased ~1.9x; average prompt size stable; completion tokens up proportional to requests. No sign of metering backfill/lag. Error rate modestly elevated around 22:00–23:00 UTC with higher stream disconnects (matches pattern from other streaming tickets).

2026-02-12 01:10Z (Priya Shah): Spot-checked 10 provided request IDs in metering logs: exactly 1 billable event per request ID; token totals within expected ranges. No evidence of double-count per request_id.

2026-02-12 02:05Z (Priya Shah -> Internal note): Hypothesis: client retries on streaming disconnect/timeout are generating *new* requests and re-consuming tokens. Customer likely perceives double-count because the user sees “one” interaction but the client made multiple generation attempts.

2026-02-12 02:20Z (Priya Shah): Shared customer-safe guidance: treat stream disconnects as retriable but ensure backoff + cap retries; increase client timeout; avoid immediate replay loops; log request IDs to correlate retries. Linked streaming troubleshooting/workaround doc and asked whether they can reduce retries temporarily to validate impact on usage.

2026-02-12 18:12Z (Customer - Aurora Search): Reduced retries to 2 and increased timeout to 60s. Usage spike started to normalize within a few hours. Still asking if Redwood can add a way to dedupe retries.

2026-02-13 00:15Z (Priya Shah): Handoff note to Platform/Billing hooks owner: while no duplication found, request for product improvement—idempotency/dedup guidance for streaming retries + better request-id logging in SDK. Looping in Dylan Brooks for internal tracking and to route to the right owner.

2026-02-13 00:31Z (Dylan Brooks): Acknowledged. No current metering duplication issue identified. Suggested adding a Support macro + docs link emphasizing idempotency/retry guidance; also noted TS SDK PR for request ID logging helper is in review (pr-488).

2026-02-14 19:08Z (Priya Shah): Customer update: confirmed billing reflects actual successful generations; spikes aligned with increased retry attempts. Recommended: keep retries low (<=2–3), exponential backoff + jitter, prefer longer timeouts for streaming, log request IDs, and avoid replaying the same user action without an idempotency strategy.

2026-02-16 16:40Z (Priya Shah): Closing as resolved—no evidence of double-counting; usage increase attributed to client retry behavior during streaming timeouts/disconnects. Added internal follow-up: ensure macros link to streaming troubleshooting and request-id logging helper once merged.
resolution: No metering/billing duplication found. Usage spike correlated with customer-side retry policy changes (higher retries + lower client timeouts) causing repeated generation attempts for the same user action during intermittent streaming disconnects/timeouts. Provided best-practice guidance and links to streaming troubleshooting; customer confirmed usage normalized after tuning retries/timeouts.
customer_facing_message: We investigated the sample request IDs you shared and confirmed billing is recording one billable usage event per request ID (no evidence of double-counting for the same request). The usage increase aligns with your recent retry/timeout changes: when a stream times out or disconnects, the client retries by issuing a new request, which results in additional generated tokens. After reducing retries and increasing the streaming timeout, your usage began normalizing. Recommended next steps: keep retries conservative (with exponential backoff), increase streaming timeouts/keepalive, and log request IDs so we can correlate retry behavior quickly if it recurs.
internal_followups: Add/update Support macro: “Usage spike due to retries/stream restarts” with a standard diagnostic ask (SDK version, retry settings, 10+ request IDs) and links to streaming troubleshooting KB.
Track SDK adoption of request-id logging helper (TS) and ensure docs reference it for Support escalations.
If repeat pattern continues across accounts, consider product-level idempotency guidance for streaming retry workflows (Docs/DevEx + Platform).
